question: How does NativeCode get a brand cited in AI answers?
answer:
[1] NativeCode is a content marketing agency that plans and writes SEO content built to rank in Google and get cited in AI answers. We build topic clusters, briefs and articles around what your buyers search, for organizations nationwide from our Atlanta base.
[2] AI SEO, also called AI search optimization, AEO or GEO, helps your site get read, trusted and cited by Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity. NativeCode is an Atlanta-based AI SEO agency that runs this work for brands nationwide, with entity work, structured data and answer-ready content.
[3] Topic clusters are groups of linked pages, one pillar and its supporting articles, that cover a subject fully enough to rank and be cited. NativeCode is an Atlanta-based team that builds topic clusters for brands nationwide, each one intent-mapped, entity-optimized, schema-wired and interlinked for Google, AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity.

question: Does NativeCode migrate stores from WooCommerce to Shopify?
answer:
[1] Yes. We map every URL on the old store, carry over content, titles and schema, and set 301 redirects before launch.
[2] NativeCode handles Shopify migration from Magento, BigCommerce, WooCommerce and Wix, with SEO-safe redirects, clean product data and supplier EDI continuity. Our Atlanta-based team plans every URL before launch so stores keep their rankings and keep shipping orders, for brands nationwide.
[3] NativeCode handles WooCommerce to Shopify migration, moving products, variations, customers, orders, reviews and blog content, with a 301 redirect for every changed URL. We are an Atlanta-based team serving companies nationwide, and we replace WordPress plugins with Shopify apps or native features so you stop managing servers and plugin updates.

question: What is llms.txt and does a site need one?
answer:
[1] The file does work reliably in one layer, and it is the layer the original proposal described: developer tooling. AI coding assistants (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and similar tools) routinely fetch /llms.
[2] Site type Recommendation Why Developer docs / API Yes, and maintain it Coding assistants actively fetch it Technical SaaS Yes Overlaps with the tooling use case Marketing site Optional, low priority Cheap to add, no demonstrated benefit Ecommerce Skip for now Product data belongs in feeds and schema
[3] llms. txt is a community proposal, not a standard, and no major AI provider has committed to reading it.
